ladder.why: The base move: walk once and turn every next pointer backwards, keeping prev, curr and next straight.

ladder.teaches: a dummy head to merge or delete
ladder.why: A dummy head and a tail pointer make merging two sorted lists a loop with no special case for the first node.
Two steps against one: the slow pointer is at the middle exactly when the fast one runs off the end.

ladder.teaches: a dummy head to merge or delete
ladder.why: A dummy before the head turns deleting the head into the same predecessor-skip as any other deletion.

ladder.teaches: a gap of k between two pointers (k-th from the end)
ladder.why: Two pointers kept n apart find the n-th node from the end in one pass, with a dummy for removing the head.
Floyd's tortoise and hare detects a cycle in O(1) space: the fast pointer must catch the slow one inside a loop.
Find the middle with fast/slow, reverse the second half in place, and compare: the first problem that combines two list moves.

ladder.teaches: a hash map plus a doubly linked list (LRU)
ladder.why: The textbook LRU cache: a hash map to nodes plus a recency-ordered doubly linked list gives O(1) get, put and eviction.

ladder.teaches: a dummy head to merge or delete
ladder.why: A hand-built queue with delete and de-duplicate drills unlinking through the predecessor while keeping head and tail correct.

ladder.teaches: a dummy head to merge or delete
ladder.why: Odd-even list with period 3: route nodes to two dummy-headed chains and join them, an OA rewiring exercise.

ladder.teaches: a hash map plus a doubly linked list (LRU)
ladder.why: An OA page-fault count that is an LRU cache in disguise: recognise it and build the map + doubly linked list.
An OA that chains three moves: reverse a prefix in place, split into two dummy-headed chains, and weave them.
Floyd's second phase: after the meeting, a pointer from the head and one from the meeting point meet at the cycle entry.
Reverse in groups of k: probe k nodes ahead, reverse the group in place, and stitch it to the previous group's tail.

notes: The linked-list pool is dominated by cache-design problems (LRU, LFU, TTL caches, in-memory databases); only the plainest LRU problems were kept. Cycle detection, the k-th-from-end gap and dummy-head deletion had no good problem in the pool, so bloomberg-remove-linked-list-elements, mygate-remove-nth-node-from-end, google-detect-linked-list-cycle and google-linked-list-cycle-entry were taken from outside every pool. amazon-process-queries-on-cart is in the pool but is a hash-map problem, not a linked list.
